title: Bind the merged gate-table zero_state to the selected PR6030 primary replay: 2.4x normal, 1.5x -O, identical RESULT.json (no new κ)
body:
**Replay-runtime tooling only. No new κ, no certificate change, no edit to any frozen file, and no change to `make frontier6030-verify`.**

## What and why

The selected replay runs DreamingOfClouds' PR6030 primary verifier (`research/p104-helper470-twin-rung-removal/verify.py`) twice, in normal and `-O` mode, each under a 600 s stage timeout. The maintainer audit recorded 228 s and 461 s for these stages. A cProfile of the normal run puts 202 of 280 profiled seconds in one function, `clifford_exact.Op.zero_state`, called 32,766 times from `local.native()`. For every gate of every call it re-evaluates `mv(G, x)` and `qvalue(Q, alpha, x, n)` over all 512 addresses.

That bottleneck was already solved for the **same compiler bytes** (SHA256 `2982ead0…0962`) by Charles Bethin's merged `research/clifford-state-performance/fast_state.py` (PR662 lineage; #2329 wires it into cold617). PR6030's chain loads a byte-identical copy from PR5827's archive chain. This PR adds no new table algorithm. Package `research/p104-6030-zero-state-cache/` binds the existing evaluator to the selected consumer:

- `run.py` runs the unchanged PR6030 `verify.py` in place. That verifier authenticates its own source chain and requires its committed `RESULT.json` byte for byte. A loader hook intercepts any module named `clifford_exact.py`, refuses bytes that do not hash to the pin, executes exactly the hashed bytes and then swaps `Op.zero_state`. After the run, every `clifford_exact` module in `sys.modules` must carry the replacement. All 14 inputs (12 PR6030 files, `fast_state.py` and the vendored compiler) are checked against `SOURCES.json` first.
- `run.py --mode differential` runs both implementations on every call and requires equal results (32,766 calls in the normal-mode replay).
- `test_equivalence.py` (about 1 s, passes on CPython 3.10-3.14) checks 1,714 random-circuit states for n = 1..9, 280 lowered children and 48 canonical frames. It rejects three mutants via the differential mismatch and refuses changed compiler bytes. Each of the 14 changed pins is refused, and so is a one-byte change to each input file.

## Result (same fixture, serial fresh processes, Apple M5 / CPython 3.12.14, shared host)

| Stage | original (s) | gate tables (s) | ratio of medians |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| normal | 120.38 (overlapped another run), 107.01 | 47.31, 47.64 | 2.39x |
| `-O` | 62.94, 62.16 | 42.03, 41.68 | 1.50x |

Together the two primary stages save about 80 s per selected replay on this host. Raw samples are in `BENCHMARK.json`. No correctness check depends on timing.

**Side observation about the existing replay.** Under `-O`, `clifford_exact.py`'s compiler self-check asserts are dropped. These include the `zero_state` comparisons in `lower_child` and `monomial`, so the optimized stage makes 8,974 zero_state calls against 32,766 in normal mode. This is not a coverage gap, because every recipe is still checked by `native_verify.equal` (which uses `require`). The two stages simply do not execute the same checks. Locally, `-O` is faster than normal, the opposite of the audit's 228 s and 461 s. This package does not explain that difference.

## Validation

```sh
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/p104-6030-zero-state-cache   # both registered commands: PASS, 165 s
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/p104-6030-zero-state-cache --check-only
python3.1{0,1,3,4} -I -B research/p104-6030-zero-state-cache/test_equivalence.py
python3.12 -I -O -B research/p104-6030-zero-state-cache/run.py --mode fast             # PASS, 41.97 s
```

An independent Codex review (read-only) raised two must-fix items, both addressed: the placeholders are filled, and the hook now executes the hashed bytes itself rather than trusting the loader. It also raised should-fix items, addressed as well: an every-copy tripwire, mutants that must hit the mismatch error, and file-byte (not only pin) invalidation. Timings were measured before those hardening edits; post-edit runs give the same times (47.49 s normal, 41.97 s `-O`).

## Not done / open

1. Opting `scripts/audit_p1046030.py` into this binding is a maintainer decision. It runs a `work/source` copy, so `TARGET` needs a parameter, and then the five-stage audit would be compared across engines byte for byte.
2. The remaining ~45 s has no single dominant function. The earlier profile points next at the orthogonality loops in `p104-productive-controller/caller.py::physical`.
3. Only macOS / CPython 3.12 was timed.

## Credit

PR6030: DreamingOfClouds (with Claude), with Douglas Colkitt's portability repair. PR5827 chain: Ali Romman and the lineage in its files. `clifford_exact.py`: icekylinx's frame-sa504 package, with Chafik Boukhalfa's native channel (PR1992) and Ali Romman's Gaussian interpreter (PR1862). `fast_state.py` and its equality proof: Charles Bethin (PR662 lineage), reused unchanged. Related prior work on this kernel: #2329 (VictorLiwentao), `research/packed-clifford-gate-tables`, `research/clifford-state-reuse`. The binding, tests and measurements were prepared by Josie Elliston with Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic) via Claude Code, in an unattended session.
